content: 1. Amisulpride and Primaquine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. If co-administration is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 2. Primaquine and Anagrelide: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 3. Anastrozole and Primaquine: Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of primaquine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 4. Apalutamide and Primaquine: Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of primaquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose of primaquine as needed. Close monitoring is required. 5. Apomorphine and Primaquine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Arformoterol and Primaquine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Aripiprazole and Primaquine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Primaquine and Arsenic Trioxide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Artemether and Primaquine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Artemether/Lumefantrine and Primaquine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Primaquine and Asenapine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Asenapine Transdermal and Primaquine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Primaquine and Atogepant: Primaquine increases the levels or effects of atogepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Atomoxetine and Primaquine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Primaquine and Avapritinib: Primaquine increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Primaquine and Axitinib: Primaquine increases the levels of axitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Primaquine and Azithromycin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Primaquine and Bedaquiline: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Bosentan and Primaquine: Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of primaquine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Primaquine and Bupivacaine Implant: Co-administration may increase the risk of methemoglobinemia. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Primaquine and Buprenorphine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 22. Buprenorphine Buccal and Primaquine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Buprenorphine Subdermal Implant and Primaquine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Buprenorphine Transdermal and Primaquine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Buprenorphine Long-Acting Injection and Primaquine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Carbamazepine and Primaquine: Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of primaquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Cenobamate and Primaquine: Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of primaquine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of primaquine as needed and monitor closely. 28. Ceritinib and Primaquine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Chloroquine and Primaquine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration may increase the risk of hemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Chlorpromazine and Primaquine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
